fn_fixint_allow_trailing.note: Byte-identical to the bincode::serialize / bincode::deserialize / bincode::serialized_size free functions. This is what trust-certify, trust-clean and trust-proof-cert use.

varint_default.note: The DOCUMENTED builder default. NO live caller uses it. Captured so a replacement cannot silently alias DefaultOptions::new() onto fixint.

fixint_reject_trailing_limit16.note: Decode-section only. Same shape as the trust-ir codec with a tiny limit so limit behaviour is observable.

instrument_mutation_evidence.note: TRANSCRIBED from the mutation harness runs, not produced by this program. It exists so a reader does not have to take on faith that the recorded bytes are really bincode's. Reproduce with the recipe below.
instrument_mutation_evidence.reproducibility: Two consecutive runs of the generator are byte-identical apart from provenance.captured_utc (the runtime's stack-overflow message carries a thread id, which the generator normalises to <tid>).

mutations.edit: cfg_varint(): DefaultOptions::new() -> DefaultOptions::new().with_fixint_encoding() (the exact 'varint silently means fixint' trap)
mutations.compared_on: --encode-only output (a wrong int encoding makes a DECODE fixture reinterpret a length prefix, and an unlimited Read-er lane then attempts that allocation; measured: the full run aborted with 'memory allocation of 7016996765293437204 bytes failed')
mutations.observed: DETECTED on 110 of 167 encode cases; varint_default hex changed, e.g. u32_251 fbfb00 -> fb000000, i32_neg1 01 -> ffffffff, string_ascii 0568656c6c6f -> 050000000000000068656c6c6f, e3_c 02 -> 02000000, bigenum_v256 fb0001 -> 00010000, u64_max fdffffffffffffffff -> ffffffffffffffff. After the mutation, varint_default equalled fn_fixint_allow_trailing on ALL 167 cases.
mutations.after_revert: encode-only output byte-identical to the baseline.

mutations.compared_on: full output (a trailing-policy change reinterprets no length, so it is allocation-safe)
mutations.observed: DETECTED on 3 of 40 decode cases; the trust_ir lane flipped from 'Slice had bytes remaining after deserialization' to ACCEPT on u32_trailing_garbage, bool_trailing_garbage, string_trailing_garbage. The encode section was unchanged, confirming trailing policy is decode-only.
mutations.after_revert: full output byte-identical to the baseline.

instrument_mutation_evidence.recipe: In the throwaway generator: apply the edit, `cargo +stable build`, re-run, diff the named section against the baseline, revert, re-run, confirm byte-identity.

derived_observations.note: Each item below is a RESTATEMENT of data recorded in this same file, with the case names that carry the evidence. Verify every claim against the named cases; nothing here is independent knowledge.

items.claim: The free functions bincode::serialize / bincode::deserialize / bincode::serialized_size are byte-for-byte the fn_fixint_allow_trailing config.
items.evidence: counts.free_fn_vs_fn_config_mismatches is empty across all encode cases.

items.claim: The two LIVE configs (fn_* and trust_ir_*) produce IDENTICAL bytes for every value. They differ only in decode-time trailing-byte policy and byte limit.
items.evidence: Compare configs.fn_fixint_allow_trailing.hex with configs.trust_ir_*.hex on every encode case.

items.claim: char is written as raw UTF-8 with NO length prefix and is self-delimiting; its width is recovered from the first byte via a UTF8_CHAR_WIDTH table.
items.evidence: encode char_a=61 (1 byte), char_4byte_gclef=f09d849e (4 bytes); decode char_invalid_first_byte_80.

items.claim: Option tags and bool bytes are written as RAW single bytes, NOT through the int encoding, so they are identical under fixint and varint.
items.evidence: encode option_u32_some fn=0107000000 var=0107; bool_true=01 in both.

items.claim: Fixed-size arrays and tuples carry NO length prefix; Vec/String/map/serde_bytes DO.
serde_bytes (serialize_bytes) and Vec<u8> (serialize_seq of u8) produce IDENTICAL bytes.
items.evidence: bytes_123 and vec_u8_123 have the same hex under every config.

items.claim: The varint single-byte ceiling is 250, not 255. 251..=65535 uses marker 0xFB + u16 LE; 0xFC = u32; 0xFD = u64; 0xFE = u128; 0xFF is a reserved extension point that always errors on decode.
items.evidence: encode u16_250 vs u16_251; decode varint_extension_byte_ff.

items.claim: Under varint, signed integers are zigzag-encoded; unsigned are not. i128::MIN and u128::MAX therefore encode to the SAME bytes.
items.evidence: encode i128_min and u128_max are both feffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff under varint_default.

items.claim: Enum variant indices go THROUGH the int encoding (u32), so they are 4 fixed bytes under fixint and varint-encoded under varint. A variant index > 255 is ordinary.

The byte limit set by with_limit() is NOT enforced when deserializing from a SLICE. internal::deserialize_seed replaces the caller's limit with Infinite. It IS enforced when deserializing from a Read-er, and it IS enforced on serialize (via a serialized_size pre-pass).
items.evidence: decode string_len20_full_payload_vs_limit16: fixint_reject_trailing_limit16 ACCEPTS a 28-byte input under a 16-byte limit, while fixint_reject_trailing_limit16__via_reader errors 'the size limit has been reached'. encode_errors vec_u8_len100_over_limit16 errors on serialize.

items.claim: One SliceReader produces TWO DIFFERENT end-of-input messages. The io::Read path yields 'io error: unexpected end of file'; the get_byte_slice path (String/Vec/bytes payloads) yields 'io error: ' with an EMPTY message, because SliceReader::unexpected_eof constructs io::Error::new(UnexpectedEof, ""). The IoReader path yields a third, 'io error: failed to fill whole buffer'.
items.evidence: decode u32_truncated_3_bytes vs string_truncated_payload vs their __via_reader lanes.

items.claim: The varint decoder does NOT require a canonical (minimal-length) encoding: the long form of a small value is accepted.
items.evidence: decode varint_noncanonical_251_for_small: input fb0100 decodes to 1 under varint_default, and re-encodes to the SHORTER 01.

items.claim: Bad enum discriminant messages are produced by serde_derive, not by bincode, so their exact text is tied to the serde version recorded in provenance. Option's tag error, by contrast, is bincode's own InvalidTagEncoding.
items.evidence: decode enum3_discriminant_99 gives 'invalid value: integer `99`, expected variant index 0 <= i < 3' (serde) while option_tag_02 gives 'tag for enum is not valid, found 2' (bincode).

items.claim: bincode 1.3.3 has NO recursion limit on decode. A hostile, highly nested input does not produce an error; it overflows the stack and ABORTS the process, which catch_unwind cannot intercept.
items.evidence: deep_decode_subprocess_probe: see which depths exit 0 with ACCEPT and which are killed by signal 6 with 'has overflowed its stack'.

items.claim: Unit, unit struct and zero-length arrays encode to ZERO bytes.
items.evidence: encode unit, unit_struct, array_u8_0 all have len 0.

items.claim: serialized_size always equals the length actually written.
Errors are Box<ErrorKind>; the Display text of each kind is what a replacement must reproduce if callers match on message text. Debug renders the ErrorKind variant name.
items.evidence: every decode entry carries both error_display and error_debug.
